description: Streamlining Inspection and Food Safety Procedures for Agricultural Food Products exported to Member Countries of the European Union
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Member countries of the European Union are coordinated under a common protection law regarding the permissible levels of pesticides/residues that may be present in food, known as Maximum Residue Levels. The Health and Food Safety Regulatory Authority, an Agency of the European Commission, has reported that the levels of agrochemical residues in certain fresh vegetables and fruits exported from Sri Lanka to the European Union member countries are significantly higher than Maximum Residue Levels by now. Therefore, the need to streamline adequate inspection and food safety procedures for Sri Lankan agricultural exports to prevent the future challenges of exporting agricultural products to the EU countries and other importing countries, has been identified. Accordingly, as an initial step, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to make it mandatory for all fresh vegetables and fruits to be exported at least only through farms, registered exporters and processing and packing plants that have been certified in accordance with the Sri Lankan Good Agricultural Practices (SLGAP) guidelines to ensure the quality of all fresh vegetables and fruits exported to the European Union.
